summary: Registering a GitHub OAuth app is free and self-serve with no provider review, so a developer can test it the same day. Any user can connect their personal account right away, but users whose organization has OAuth app access restrictions on must wait for an organization owner to approve the app before it can reach that organization's private data.
timeToProduction: Same day for personal accounts; org-owned data depends on each organization owner's approval, which the docs give no timing for

gates.title: Anyone with a GitHub account can register the app
Tokens share a 5,000 requests per hour limit per user
gates.what: OAuth tokens count against the authorizing user's primary limit of 5,000 requests per hour, shared with that user's personal access tokens and other apps. Access tokens do not expire by default; expiring tokens are opt-in. Each user can hold 10 tokens per app and scope combination.
gates.where: Developer settings, OAuth apps, your app: the expiry setting is 'Expire user access tokens' at registration. The rate limit is not configurable by you.
gates.todo: Pace requests using the x-ratelimit-* response headers, and decide whether to enable expiring tokens before launch because existing tokens stay long-lived.

gates.title: No app review for OAuth apps
gates.what: The docs describe no review for an OAuth app to authorize users. Review and publisher verification apply only to GitHub Marketplace listings, and only paid plans require verification.

gates.title: Organization owners must approve your app before members can use it on org data
gates.what: New organizations have OAuth app access restrictions enabled by default. Members cannot authorize your app for organization resources until an owner approves it. Personal account access is not affected.
gates.where: Organization owner acts: Organization Settings, Third-party Access, OAuth app policy, then Review and Grant access.
gates.todo: Tell target organization owners in advance to approve the app, and make your sign-in flow handle users who are not yet approved.

gates.title: No paid plan needed for the API
Rate limits and token rules apply after launch
gates.what: Organization owners can revoke your app's access at any time. If you ever list on Marketplace with a paid plan, you must handle plan-change webhooks.
gates.where: Organization owner acts: OAuth app policy in organization settings.
gates.todo: Handle 403 and 429 responses with retry-after and reset headers, and handle a revoked token gracefully.

requirements.text: A GitHub account with admin access to the organizations you want to test against
A homepage URL and one or more callback URLs (up to 10), using only public information
A decision on whether you need the device flow (headless apps) and whether to enable expiring tokens

steps.text: Sign in to GitHub and open Settings, then Developer settings, then OAuth apps.
steps.detail: Use the account or organization that should own the app; you can also register under an org you administer.

steps.text: Click New OAuth App and enter the application name, homepage URL, and optional description.
steps.detail: Do not put internal URLs in these fields; they are public.
Up to 10 callback URLs. Leave wildcard matching off unless you need it.

steps.text: Decide on device flow and expiring tokens before registering.
steps.detail: Device flow is only for headless apps and must be enabled in settings. 'Expire user access tokens' is on by default; turn it off only if your code does not yet handle refresh tokens.

steps.text: Click Register application and copy the client ID and client secret.
steps.detail: Never put the client secret in client-side or device code.

steps.text: Draft the list of scopes and the privacy wording the app needs.
steps.detail: Scopes are set in the authorization request, not in the app settings.

steps.text: Test by signing in with your own personal account.
steps.detail: Personal accounts can authorize right away.

steps.text: Ask each target organization owner to approve the app under OAuth app policy.
steps.detail: Members and outside collaborators cannot authorize org data until an owner grants access.

steps.text: Confirm that a member of an approved organization can sign in and see org data.

blockers.problem: Org members see an error or cannot authorize the app for organization repositories.
blockers.fix: Have the organization owner approve the app under OAuth app policy, or check whether the org has restrictions on.

blockers.problem: Authorized users get a token that stops working after eight hours.
blockers.fix: Expiring tokens were enabled. Store the refresh token and use the refresh flow; the refresh token expires after six months without use.

blockers.problem: Requests start failing with 403 or 429 errors.
blockers.fix: Check the x-ratelimit-reset and retry-after headers, and back off instead of retrying immediately.
Turn on Enable Device Flow in the app settings.

blockers.problem: Changing the callback URL fails for a callback that worked before.
blockers.fix: Check whether wildcard matching is on for that callback, and whether the redirect_uri matches it exactly.

couldNotVerify: Wait times for organization owners to approve an app; the docs give none.
Whether the 'Review OAuth apps', 'Privileged apps' and 'Third-party applications' docs add review or approval steps; I did not read them.
Whether a GitHub Enterprise Cloud org gives a higher rate limit for an OAuth app you own; the rate limit page states this but I did not confirm how to apply it.
The 200-user minimum for OAuth apps on Marketplace paid listings, and whether it applies to unlisted apps.

claims.statement: Any GitHub user can register an OAuth app under a personal account or under an organization they administer.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.

claims.statement: Registering an OAuth app involves no provider review step.
claims.note: Inferred: the registration steps and the authorization docs describe no review; the review pages were not read.

claims.statement: Personal account users can authorize an OAuth app with no organization approval.
claims.sourceTitle: About OAuth app access restrictions - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources.

claims.statement: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions must approve an app before members can use it on org data.
claims.sourceTitle: Approving OAuth apps for your organization - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators must request approval from an organization owner before they can authorize an OAuth app that has access to the organization's resources.

claims.statement: OAuth tokens count against the authorizing user's primary rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
claims.sourceTitle: Rate limits for the REST API - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

claims.statement: Access tokens are long-lived unless expiring tokens are enabled; expiring access tokens last eight hours and refresh tokens expire after six months without use.
claims.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

claims.statement: Marketplace listings require review and acceptance of the Marketplace Developer Agreement; only paid plans require organization publisher verification.
claims.sourceTitle: Requirements for listing an app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: To publish a paid plan for your app on the GitHub Marketplace, your app must be owned by an organization that is a verified publisher.

claims.statement: Organizations created new have OAuth app access restrictions enabled by default.
claims.sourceTitle: About OAuth app access restrictions - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default.

claims.statement: Owners approve apps under Organization Settings, Third-party Access, OAuth app policy, Review, then Grant access; approval timing is not stated.
claims.sourceTitle: Approving OAuth apps for your organization - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: In the "Third-party Access" section of the sidebar, click OAuth app policy .

claims.statement: The OAuth API and app registration are free; a paid plan is only needed to sell on Marketplace.
claims.sourceTitle: Requirements for listing an app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: Free apps are encouraged in GitHub Marketplace and are a great way to offer open source services.
claims.note: Pricing of the API itself is not stated on the pages; it is treated as free based on the registration docs.

claims.statement: Organization owners can revoke an app's access at any time.
claims.note: Inferred from the restrictions page, which says owners can remove access; the exact wording was not copied.

claims.statement: Registration asks for name, homepage URL, optional description, up to 10 callback URLs, device flow toggle, and expiring-token toggle, then Register application.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

claims.statement: Device flow must be enabled in app settings before use, or the device_flow_disabled error occurs.
claims.quote: Before you can use the device flow to authorize and identify users, you must first enable it in your app's settings.

claims.statement: Wildcard matching for callback URLs is a security risk and should be off unless needed.
claims.quote: Only enable wildcard matching if you absolutely need it and you are entirely certain that you control all possible subdomains and paths of the callback URL.

claims.statement: Exceeding a rate limit returns 403 or 429, and retries should wait until the reset or retry-after time.
claims.sourceTitle: Rate limits for the REST API - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: If you exceed your primary rate limit, you will receive a 403 or 429 response, and the x-ratelimit-remaining header will be 0 .
